title: Three steps to synthetic long stock with a deep ITM call
summary: Step one: a long call and a short put at the same strike replicate stock. Step two: move the call down to 95 delta or more. Step three: do not sell the put, because it pays very little and carries the big downside. Without the put, losses slow as the call delta falls in a crash.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $200. Goal: long stock exposure built with options.
Step 1: buy a call and sell a put at the same strike and expiry. The gold line is stock exposure, synthetically.
Steps 2 and 3: keep only a 95+ delta call. The blue line tracks the stock above the strike.
The violet gap is the value of NOT selling the put: below the strike your losses stop, the put's would not.
Through time the call lags the stock a little: you pay a small extrinsic value instead of collecting a tiny put premium.
Breakeven is the strike plus the premium paid. One downside: calls do not collect dividends.

takeaways: Long call + short put at one strike = synthetic long stock (put-call parity).
A 95+ delta call behaves like stock but its maximum loss is the premium paid.
Size by total delta: one deep ITM contract is close to 100 shares of exposure.
caveats: Deep ITM premium is large; per-name premium caps on NLV limit the size.

backtest.note: Six-month 95-delta call, rolled at 60 days to expiry; 30% of the strategy capital per position.
